# webrtc-bridge

webrtc for the vault worker. a worker has no `RTCPeerConnection`, so a tab makes the real one and the worker drives it with messages. hyper-webrtc gets its `RTCPeerConnection` from `get-webrtc`, and `lib/build-vault.js` swaps `get-webrtc` for this module in the worker bundle.

```js
// worker (lib/vault-worker.js)
const webrtc = require('webrtc-bridge')
webrtc.use_page(port)  // this tab does the webrtc from now on (the first tab that is still open)
webrtc.drop_page(port) // the tab closed, its connections close too

// page (lib/datashell.js)
const serve_webrtc = require('webrtc-bridge/page')
serve_webrtc(port, { transfer: !globalThis.SharedWorker })
```

## how it works

- `webrtc-bridge.js` (worker) has only what hyper-webrtc uses, `RTCPeerConnection` with its setup calls and `onicecandidate`, `RTCIceCandidate`, and its one negotiated data channel. each call goes to `page.js` in the tab, which runs it on the real connection
- the data channel stays in the tab and every message is forwarded to the worker and back, or with `transfer: true` the tab transfers the channel into the worker, then the data goes from the worker straight to the other browser. transfer only works into a dedicated worker, chrome 156 and firefox 160 drop a channel sent to a SharedWorker (tested 15 nov), so only the vault fallback without SharedWorker uses it
- one data channel message can be at most 256KB in chrome, so every message goes in 16KB pieces, each starts with one byte that says if more pieces follow, and the other side joins them again (`pieces.js`, both ways use it)

## how a connection becomes webrtc

- hyperswarm and the dht run in the vault worker, over the relay websocket. with `custodial: false` the noise handshake is in the worker too, so every connection there is our noise stream through the relay
- on a new connection both sides say on a protomux channel (`hyper-webrtc/upgrade`) if theyre a browser or native (`upgrade_connection` in identity-networking). if both are browsers the worker runs `HyperWebRTC.from(socket)`
- hyper-webrtc sends the webrtc offer, answer and ice candidates over that same noise stream (`hyper-webrtc/signal`), so the relay connection does the signaling. if the relay stream closes the webrtc connection closes too, and the other way round
- the `RTCPeerConnection` hyper-webrtc gets in the worker is this module, every call goes to the tab with 📡 in its title, which runs it on the real one (see how it works above)

## when the tab closes

the vault swarm lives in the worker, only the webrtc connections need a tab. when the tab that does the webrtc closes, its connections close, the worker gives the job to the next open tab and hyperswarm connects again through it. tested with 2 browsers in chrome, a post still arrived after the first tab closed
